summary: Norbert Brox (1935–2006) was a scholar in religious studies and history/archaeology. He held posts at the University of Graz (~1969–1975) and the University of Regensburg (~1975–2003).

Norbert Samuelson (1936–2022) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Northwestern University, Hebrew Union College, and Indiana University Bloomington under Shlomo Pines. He held major appointments at Temple University (1975–1998) and Arizona State University (~1998–2022).

Noriaki Hakamaya (b. 1943) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Shun'ei Hirai and Zuiho Yamaguchi. His career included posts at Komazawa Junior College and Komazawa University (1975–2011).

Noriaki Hosoda (b. 1957) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Hokkaido University, attested as assistant in 1986 and associate professor in 2003, and is attested as professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.
Noriaki Inoue (b. 1929) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1949–1953). He served as a professor at Taisho University, attested in 1982.

Norihiko Tanaka (b. 1944) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Osaka Kyoiku University, Bukkyo University, and Visva-Bharati University. He spent his academic career at Bukkyo University, serving successively as lecturer, associate professor, professor, and professor emeritus (2015–2021).
Norihiko Uchida (b. 1932) works in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Yutaka Ochihara and served as an assistant at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, attested in 1962.
Norihiro Matsuura is a scholar in history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. Matsuura is attested as a faculty member at Otani University and the Otani Academic Society in 2026.

Norihisa Baba (b. 1973) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo under Masahiro Shimoda. Baba has held positions at the University of Tokyo since 2006, becoming professor in 2019.

Norio Fujisawa (1925–2004) was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University (~1944–1953). He held posts at Kyoto University (~1960–1989) and served as director of the Kyoto National Museum (~1992–2001).
Norio Harada (b. 1919) is a scholar in Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Ryukoku University and served as a professor at Kyoto Women's University, attested in 1964.
Norio Koyama (1960–2017) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami, and served as a professor at Taisho University, attested in 2014.

Noritoshi Aramaki (b. 1936) is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He held professorial and teaching posts at Kyoto University, Osaka University, the Institute for Research in Humanities at Kyoto University, and Otani University.

Noriyuki Kudo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Bukkyo University. Kudo held positions at Bukkyo University, the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology, and Soka University, where Kudo is attested as professor in 2026.

Norman Fischer (b. 1946) is a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar. He studied at Colgate University, the University of Iowa, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union, and under Sojun Mel Weitsman and Richard Baker, later founding the Everyday Zen Foundation.

Norvin J. Hein (1914–2017) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Franklin Edgerton. He served as associate professor of comparative religion at Yale University Divinity School, attested in 1965.

Yoshinari Fuji is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University. Fuji held posts at Daegu University, Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, Bukkyo University, and served as professor of Buddhist studies at Ryukoku University (attested 2011–2013).

Notto R. Thelle (b. 1941) is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He served as associate director at the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions (1974) and held a post at the University of Oslo (~1986–2006).

Noémie Verdon is an Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Lausanne under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand. She held a post at Kyoto University, attested in 2019.

Noël Péri (1865–1922) worked in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He taught Western music at Tokyo Fine Arts School (1896–1906) and served at the École française d'Extrême-Orient as a resident (1907) and secretary-librarian (1911).
